title: Dud Bascomb as an underrated trumpeter
summary: Hawkins praises Dud's ideas and notes his solo on 'Tuxedo Junction'.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What, I'm just trying to think of any other trumpet players that you knew at that time that were either colleagues or influences, or sort of all doing the same thing and bringing it together that you remember?
You was calling it, you was doing all right by calling those names there.
Well, okay. Let's not leave Dud out.
Oh, yeah. I thought we, yeah.
That's like cause I'm saying yeah Dud too, cause....
See, from school out there, you know that, you know that Dud and myself were close.
And I had a lot, and I cared for his playing very much so. Cause we was, he had very beautiful ideas.
Yeah, that's what I wanted to reflect on because we were speaking of him as one of your, you know, growing up buddies and all like that.
But, I mean, really, I think as a trumpet player, he was sort of underrated, you know?
And, I wondered what your feelings were.

cause he had, you know, beautiful ideas. That solo we played in 'Tuxedo Junction.' You know, just right out of nowhere. He used to play that way in school. I saw him that way in school. And, he used to tell me about it. He'd say, 'Hawk, you're the best first chair man I know of.' And, we used to compliment each other on certain things we did. You know? And like I said, we was roommates. And, we got our different ideas this way. That's the way he felt, and that's the way he played. And, he had beautiful ideas. I'll tell you another trumpet player we didn't do. Hot Lips Page?
